verdict: Caution: lend selectively to integrated layer and broiler units with feed control and monthly stock-and-sales reporting; avoid thin-net-worth partnership farms and any unit with ration-rice or feed-diversion exposure.
title: Salem Poultry Farming: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A Salem poultry unit buys feed, day-old chicks or layer birds, and converts them into eggs or broiler meat sold wholesale to grocery shops, speciality markets, bakeries and fast-food outlets.** In the Namakkal-to-Krishnagiri belt, eggs move by lorry and tempo and are sold wholesale, with retail shops selling an egg at Rs.6 [1]. Feed is the dominant cost and the bird is the inventory; cash arrives on wholesale settlement cycles, not at the farm gate. **So when a proposal lands, check the offtake list first: named wholesale buyers with repeat volumes matter more than the shed count.**

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in feed conversion and bird weight, not in the shed.** Peer results show the swing: Venky's Q4 FY26 broiler meat realisation peaked at INR 102.67/kg, April FY27 ran INR 97-100/kg, and DOC prices fell from a ~INR 55 peak to INR 21-22 in parts of North India by mid-May [4]. SKM Egg's Q2 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR 28 crores from INR 38 crores on higher feed raw material cost [7]. **So when a proposal lands, ask for the last six months of feed cost per kg of bird or per egg; if the borrower cannot produce it, collect from customer.**

## What has changed now
**Local demand has softened: re-intensified heat has cut egg consumption in Salem and prices have fallen [1].** That is a June 2025 report and is now old, so treat it as direction, not current price. **If a proposal shows feed cost materially below the district norm, ask where the feed comes from and inspect the feed store.**

## Who to pursue, and how to grow safely
**Pursue layer farms with contracted wholesale offtake and broiler units attached to a hatchery or feed mill; avoid partnership farms with modest net worth.** Sree Renuka Poultry's Rs.12.25 Cr net worth and partnership constitution constrained its flexibility [11], and Srinivasa Farms ran a 1.08x current ratio, 0.45x quick ratio, 89% limit utilisation and negative Rs.28 crore cash flow from operations [8]. **Structure against the cycle: monthly stock-and-sales statements, feed bills, and a drawing-power limit tied to bird/egg inventory; take the buyer ledger every month.** Longer shelf life of frozen meat partly shields realisations [9], so favour units with cold storage. ## Early-warning signs
**Watch feed bills against bird count, buyer concentration, and limit utilisation.** If feed purchase per bird falls while sales hold, ask for the feed store and purchase invoices. If one buyer crosses a third of sales, ask for the contract. If utilisation runs near the 89% seen at Srinivasa [8], stop enhancement and re-size the limit.
